copies.headline: Still Number One, Suddenly Mortal
copies.body: Adam is 6-2 with a 66-22 all-play, 75 percent, best in the league, and 139.6 a game, also first. That's not a hot start, that's a résumé. The two-week slide is real though — 103.0 in Week 7 was his season low, and the last three weeks he's all-play 52 percent, sixth. The roster still projects 134 a week, first of twelve, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Kenneth Walker III anchoring it, and 139 projected against Grant. Mr. Consistent being mildly inconsistent is the only story here.

copies.headline: John's 80-Grade Draft Keeps Outrunning Itself
copies.body: The draft-night roster scored 80 out of 100, T-9th of 12, and John has turned it into 133.0 points a game, 2nd of 12. That's not luck — luck has him at minus-0.5 wins, meaning 5-3 understates him. The all-play is 61-27, 69%, also 2nd. Last three weeks: 100.1, 127.7, 165.1, a 24-9 all-play stretch. Puka Nacua projects 24, Brock Bowers 18, and the lineup profiles at 127 a week, 3rd of 12. He gets Mitchell with a 133 projection. Peter leads this series 6-3 all-time the other way; John's just quietly better right now.

copies.headline: Christian Keeps Scoring, Keeps Losing, Keeps Waiting
copies.body: A 3-5 team with the 3rd-best scoring average in the league and a 54-34 all-play is not a bad team, it's a mugging victim. Christian is 1.9 wins below expectation, which is the statistical version of getting your lunch taken every Sunday. The draft graded T-2nd at 89, and the roster still projects 131 a week, 2nd of 12, with Lamb, Kittle and Chase Brown doing honest work. Last three weeks: 124.3, 122.3, 123.5, a metronome. Week 9 projects 134 against Kaleb. Eventually math pays.

copies.headline: Logan Is 3-5 And Playing Great
copies.body: The record says 3-5. Everything else says otherwise: 122.4 a game, 4th of 12, an all-play mark of 54-34 that's T-3rd, and 1,075.7 points against — nobody in this league has been shot at harder. Luck sits at -1.9 wins. Over the last three weeks he's gone 152.5, 118.9, 146.4 and posted a 27-6 all-play, best in the league. The man who took the top seed twice and won nothing is now scoring like a contender with a losing record. The roster only projects 117, 8th of 12, so Burrow and Jefferson have to keep carrying.

copies.headline: 6-2 Built On Fumes And Favorable Schedules
copies.body: Leif is 6-2 with a four-game win streak and an all-play record of 43-45, which is the gap between a good team and a lucky one. The luck column says +2.1 wins, first-luckiest of 12. The last three weeks: 112.3, 92.9, then 64.7, an all-play of 10-23 over that stretch. His draft-night roster graded 80, 12th of 12, and he's been outrunning it ever since. Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans and David Montgomery are all questionable. Noah's next, and Noah doesn't miss when it counts.

copies.headline: Grant Is Exactly What The Numbers Say
copies.body: Grant is 4-4, all-play 42-46, luck +0.2 — a team so precisely average it's almost a statement. The 918.3 points for ranks 6th of 12, the scoring average is 114.8, and the power score lands at 48.6. There is no scam here and no hidden gem. The problem is what's coming: a roster index of 39 and a projection of 113 a week, 10th of 12, with Amon-Ra St. Brown doing heavy lifting and Christian Watson and Kyler Murray both questionable. Week 9 is Adam. Good luck.

copies.headline: CJ Climbs While Scoring Less Than Ever
copies.body: CJ moved up two spots on the strength of other people's failures, which is the most Taylor Gang thing imaginable. The last three weeks: 125.5, then 90.9, then 95.1, an all-play of 12-21 over that stretch — 36 percent, T-9th of 12. The season average is 111.2, 8th of 12, and the 40-48 all-play says 4-4 is exactly what he's earned. The backfield is real — Jonathan Taylor at 20 projected, Chuba Hubbard at 18 — but Tyler Shough at 15 is the ceiling problem. Logan's next, 114 projected.

copies.headline: Isaac Is 4-4 On Vibes Alone
copies.body: Two straight wins, and Isaac is climbing on a roster that still averages 104.8 per game, 11th of 12. The all-play tells the real story: 31-57, 35%, also 11th. That's not a contender, that's a guy +1.2 wins over expected riding the fourth-luckiest schedule in the league. The confusing part is the talent — Ja'Marr Chase, Malik Nabers, Saquon Barkley, and a lineup projecting 124 a week, 5th of 12. Week 6's 79.0 shouldn't be possible with that roster. Peter's next. Start scoring like the names suggest.

copies.headline: Best Draft, Worst Projection, Living On Luck
copies.body: Peter drafted the best board in the league on paper — 89 out of 100, first of twelve — and has turned it into a roster that projects 100 a week, twelfth of twelve. The 5-3 record is a costume: all-play 40-48, luck +1.4 wins, third-luckiest in the league. The last three weeks tell it straight: 69.8, 114.6, 118.1, a 36% all-play clip. Lamar Jackson is OUT, A.J. Brown and Kyle Monangai questionable, and Justin Herbert projects 12. The 2022 champ is being carried by points against, not points.

copies.headline: Noah's January Form Arrives Three Months Early
copies.body: Noah finally cleared 140 for the first time all season, and it moved him exactly one spot. That's what 2-6 buys you. The all-play is 33-55, 38%, 10th of 12 — this isn't a scheduling conspiracy, it's a 107.5 per game offense that bottomed out at 79.6 in Week 3. The last three weeks are genuinely better, 58% all-play, 5th of 12. The draft night roster graded 86, T-4th, which makes the 2-6 more annoying, not less. The postseason assassin has to reach the postseason first. Leif's next, 121 projected.

copies.headline: 5-3 On The Thinnest Possible Evidence
copies.body: Kaleb is 5-3 and the schedule gets all the credit: 103.4 points a game, 12th of 12, and 805.8 points against, the fewest in the league. The all-play says 34-54, 39%, 9th of 12. The luck column says +1.9 wins, 2nd-highest. Week 8 was 62.7, a season low, and the roster index of 22 says the bailout isn't coming — Goff, Jeanty, London and a questionable Breece Hall project this thing at 104 a week. The 86 draft grade, T-4th, has aged into a cautionary tale. Christian's next.

copies.headline: Nico Found, Everything Else Still Missing
copies.body: Mitchell's roster projects for 124 a week, 4th of 12, and he's averaging 106.9. That gap is the whole season. The all-play is 30-58, 12th of 12, and the last three weeks are 5-28 — 85.5, 79.4, 108.5 while Jahmyr Gibbs, Dak Prescott and Nico Collins all sit on his roster. Luck is -1.7, so there's a sliver of sympathy available, but a team that scores 73.0 in Week 2 earns most of its 1-7. Week 9 projects 127 against John. Start the right nine.

intro: Adam holds the top spot and it isn't close: 139.6 per game, a 75% all-play, and a 6-2 record built on zero luck, which is the rudest part of it. Mitchell sits at the bottom at 1-7 with a 15% form rating, though 106.9 per game and a 127 projection next week say he's been beaten up more than he's been bad — his -1.7 luck is the second-worst on the board. The week's ugliest slide belongs to Kaleb, who dropped from 8th to 11th while somehow still carrying a 5-3 record; 103.4 points per game and +1.9 luck is a house built on sand. Leif's fall from 3rd to 5th is the same story with better wallpaper: 6-2, 49% all-play, and a 30% form number that's heading the wrong direction.
